biography.plain_text: Robert Ian 'Bob' Oatley was an Australian wine entrepreneur who built Rosemount Estate after trading Papua New Guinean coffee and cocoa. He also established Robert Oatley Vineyards, continuing his family's involvement in winemaking.

long_biography.plain_text:
Wine entrepreneur Bob Oatley helped bring John Webber's portrait of Captain James Cook back to Australia for the National Portrait Gallery. His friends Gordon and Marilyn Darling introduced him to the acquisition, and he travelled to London to see the painting before contributing. He became a founding benefactor of the gallery, supplying wine for its public events throughout his remaining life.

A successful competitive sailor, Oatley also equipped Australia's Olympic sailing programme. Before the Beijing Games, he bought four 470-class boats for the team. He provided Australia's national sailing association with a Sydney building rent-free for three years.
